item.title: Argentinian footballer Lionel Messi announces his retirement
item.description:
The Argentine’s career with Argentina was singular, and his exit is a reminder that all good things come to an end IIt was among the defining moments of the 2026 World Cup: Lionel Messi standing arms akimbo, looking up towards Argentina’s fervent supporters after losing the final . Tears streamed down his face after his team’s embarrassing loss to Spain in what we now know was Messi’s final match wearing that famous Argentina kit. It was not the first time he’d cried at the tournament. There had been tears of joy in Argentina’s opening match, when Messi rolled back the clock to his glory days with a trio of spectacular goals against Algeria. There had been more when his brace against Austria pushed Argentina through to the knockout round as group winners, and even more when his equalizer against Egypt threw la Albiceleste a much-needed lifeline. item.title: Nepal disaster: fake and AI images flood social media as deaths mount
item.description:
Roughly 160 people are dead and hundreds more — including dozens of international tourists — are missing after flash floods hit a region on the mountainous border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday. Devastating footage posted to social media shows people fleeing a wall of water that washed away buildings and vehicles. Initial analysis of satellite imagery and reports from the Nepalese government indicate that the flooding was likely triggered by a landslide caused after a piece of a glacier fell hundreds of feet. As the region warms, its ice is becoming increasingly unstable , raising the risk of catastrophic flooding. “The glaciers over there are definitely in retreat,” said Joseph Shea, an associate professor of geography at the University of Northern British Columbia. “There’s a lot of glacier mass up there, but we’re seeing thinning, we’re seeing retreating.” Since 2000, the world’s…

item.title: Tariffs spat: Carney bets Canada can defy Trump
item.description:
Meanwhile, Trump posts video of himself kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with Lake America sign Donald Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel on Saturday over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the Ontario premier erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting a video of him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA. Rhetoric over the naming of Lake Ontario is the public face of an escalating trade dispute between the US and its northern neighbor involving a 50% US tariff on Canadian steel and retaliatory tariffs from Ottawa. item.title: Putin, Xi reaffirm Russia-China ties amid ‘unpredictable’ world
item.description:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping pledged stronger ties with Russia after meeting President Vladimir Putin on Monday, as Beijing flexed its diplomatic might at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan. With 10 member states in attendance, the gathering offers Xi the chance to demonstrate that Beijing has “ friends and options around the world at precisely the moment Washington is alienating many of its allies,” a China adviser in the Biden administration told The New York Times. It’s also a chance for Xi to put a floor under China’s tense relationship with India, which “finds itself a reluctant and defensive participant — unable to move too close to China or identify fully with the anti-Western agenda promoted by Beijing and Moscow,” a Foreign Policy columnist argued. — Brendan Ruberry

Sources: Al Jazeera English, Deutsche Welle, Semafor

item.title: Dolly Forever
item.description:
Kristof Ramon, Cor Vos There are no guarantees in sport. A race is never really over until it's over. Nothing lasts forever. Bike racing fans hold these truths to be self evident. Our aphorisms are as fundamental as they are cliché, hardly even worth writing down – but for the last few years, Tadej Pogačar has made us question every one of them and so much more of what we thought we knew about bike racing. Throughout the most dominant stretch in modern cycling history, all but the flattest events on the calendar have seemed like foregone conclusions the moment the UAE Team Emirates-XRG leader decided to take to the start line. And from the moment he put the hammer down in the very first week of this or that race, it really was over for everyone else. At times, this era of inevitability has felt like it might never end. item.title: Data from 911 calls at ICE detention centers must be released under bill going to Gov. Newsom
item.description:
In summary The California Legislature passed a bill that would force disclosure of information about emergency calls at immigrant detention centers. A Democratic lawmaker put it forward after reading news stories in CalMatters. Legislation that would improve public access to information about violence, medical emergencies, and other serious incidents in privately operated detention facilities in California is now heading to the governor’s desk. It would require local agencies to release audio and records of 911 calls and other emergency-service calls originating from the facilities upon request. State Sen. item.title: Hiker, 91, becomes oldest person to complete grueling Appalachian Trail
item.description:
Dale Sanders said he fell 71 times on the trail, but completed the journey as ‘people are motivated … by my efforts’ A 91-year-old hiker has reclaimed his record as the oldest person to complete the more than 2,000-mile Appalachian Trail. By his count, Dale Sanders, of Tennessee, fell 71 times during the feat, six of which he said were hard falls and one which required a brief hospitalization and another just 200 yards from the end. The 2,193-mile trail runs between Springer Mountain in Georgia and Mount Katahdin in Maine. Continue reading...
